assignments.node_id: כשיזכיר את עצמו שרוצה למסר נפשו על קדוש השם
assignments.reason: This is the practical eitza of the Torah — the act of reminding oneself of one's willingness for mesiras nefesh. Its essential nature is kiddush Hashem/self-sacrifice, which IS the core identity of Package 1. The Torah says this practice awakens bechinas shalom/Yosef. Though it *produces* the connection of thought to speech, the act itself IS mesiras nefesh — placing it squarely in the kiddush Hashem domain.

The joining of mind (mochin/chokhmah = chasadim) and speech (dibur = gevurot) IS the definition of shalom in this Torah. The text states explicitly: 'shalom, bechinas Yosef, shehu bechinas hitchabrut hamoach vehadibur.' This concept is not merely about speech or wisdom — it IS the synthesis of the two poles, which is the essential nature of shalom/Yosef (Package 1). The companion node 'חכמה והדבור' is already in Package 1 for the same reason.

assignments.node_id: כשמרצה למסר נפשו על קדוש השם
assignments.reason: The willingness to give one's life for kiddush Hashem IS mesiras nefesh, which IS kiddush Hashem, which IS bechinas shalom/Yosef. The Torah states: 'techef keshemurtzeh limsor nafsho al kiddush Hashem, nit'orer bechinas shalom, bechinas Yosef.' The essential nature of this concept is self-sacrifice for God's name — the very center of Package 1.

This verse-concept ('Boneh Yerushalayim Hashem') encapsulates the entire Torah's synthesis: YHVH (= mochin, Package 2) building Yerushalayim (= dibur, Package 3). While its components belong to different packages, the composite concept represents the union itself — the joining of mochin and dibur, which IS shalom. The text explains: 'lizkhot lekasher hamoach el hadibur, shezehu bechinas Boneh Yerushalayim Hashem, shehamochin bonin hadibur dikdusha.' This synthesis-concept belongs in the synthesis-package (Package 1), just as 'חכמה והדבור' and 'התחברות חסדים וגבורות' are already there.

assignments.node_id: יוכל להתפלל ולקשר המחשבה אל הדבור וכנ"ל
assignments.reason: The ability to pray and connect thought to speech is fundamentally about speech functioning in holiness. Prayer (tefillah) is the primary domain of dibur — holy speech directed to God. While the *cause* of this ability is shalom (Package 1), the concept itself IS prayer/speech — the outward, expressive faculty. Its essential nature is the speech domain: Package 3.

Speaking words in holiness and purity — this IS holy dibur, the functioning of the speech faculty with kedusha and tahara. The essential nature is speech: Package 3. Though shalom (Package 1) is required to achieve this, the concept itself describes the state of the dibur when it operates properly.
Speaking words in holiness — a variant formulation of holy speech. Same essential nature as 'יכול לדבר דבורים בקדשה ובטהרה.' The concept IS dibur in its holy state: Package 3.

assignments.node_id: יכולין לדבר, דהינו לקשר המחשבה אל הדבור
assignments.reason: The ability to speak, defined as connecting thought to speech — this IS the actualization of the speech faculty. The text equates 'being able to speak' with 'connecting machshava to dibur,' which is the proper functioning of dibur receiving from mochin. The essential nature is speech actualized: Package 3.

Connecting thought to speech — the outward, expressive function of linking the inner faculty (mochin) to the outer faculty (dibur). While it involves mochin (Package 2), the concept describes the operation from the perspective of the dibur receiving and expressing what the moach sends. In this Torah, this IS the 'building of Yerushalayim' — the speech domain being constructed and activated. Essential nature: dibur/speech functionality: Package 3.

assignments.node_id: נכנסין כל הנדחין מקדשת ישראל לתוך הקדשה
assignments.reason: The return of scattered Jews into holiness through kiddush Hashem. The text explicitly identifies this as bechinas mesiras nefesh al kiddush Hashem: 'nidchei Yisrael yekanes — zeh bechinas mesiras nefesh al kiddush Hashem.' The additions file already places the related concept 'נדחי ישראל' in Package 1 for the same reason. The essential nature of this gathering-in IS the kiddush Hashem/self-sacrifice dynamic that defines Package 1.
